content.title: About
content.content: Canned shrimp are peeled and deveined marine crustaceans packed in a sealed tin with brine or oil. They retain a delicate sea flavor, are shelf‑stable, and ready to use in salads, appetizers, pastas, and soups.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp are one of the most consumed seafood items worldwide, with over 150 million tonnes harvested each year.
Canning extends the shelf life of shrimp up to three years while preserving taste and texture.
The majority of canned shrimp come from Asian producers, especially Thailand, Vietnam, and India.
Shrimp are high in protein but low in calories – about 70 kcal per 100 g of product.
Brine often contains citric acid to keep the shrimp pink and fresh‑tasting.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Shrimp provide roughly 20 g of high‑quality protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many seafoods, canned shrimp contain very little saturated fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium is a potent antioxidant that aids immune function and thyroid health.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for red blood cell formation and nervous system maintenance.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids in shrimp help lower triglycerides and improve vascular tone.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, including anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned shrimp are often packed in salty brine, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Heavy metal residues
items.content: Seafood can accumulate cadmium and mercury; choose reputable brands that test for contaminants.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Certain cans may contain preservatives or flavor enhancers that some sensitive individuals prefer to avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned shrimp can be eaten straight from the jar, tossed into salads, mixed with pasta, added to rice dishes, or used as a topping for sandwiches. For extra flavor, quickly sauté them with garlic and lemon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened can in a cool, dry place. Once opened, transfer shrimp to an airtight container and refrigerate, consuming within 2–3 days.
